core_obligations: Derive the full collision-tree/marked-partition representation from the nonlinear recursion.
Use equality of one-site marginals to eliminate all singleton leaf blocks before estimating mismatch; an indiscriminate sum over all leaves would not yield contraction.
Control leaves retaining two coordinates by their depth-dependent nonseparation probability, then compute the exact time-mixture tree weight to obtain rate1-r(nu).

proof_roadmap.step: Symmetrize the collision law, build the Wild recurrence, and turn each marked binary tree into a product over a random partition of coordinates.
Optimal leaf coupling plus singleton-block cancellation reduces the difference to leaves holding at least two coordinates; a pair union bound weights each leaf by(r(nu)/2)^depth.
Condition the tree law at its first split to get a renewal equation; the expected weight solves zeta-prime=-(1-r)zeta. Combine with TV duality.

difficulty_reason: After ordinary finite ODE/coupling background, the task still has to design and exploit the marked collision-tree representation, cancel singleton contributions using equal marginals, and average the surviving pair weight exactly over random binary trees. The resulting contraction between two nonlinear evolutions is not a direct Markov semigroup contraction or a consequence of the old entropy-production inequality. This nonroutine combinatorial-probabilistic mechanism supports H2, subject to independent review.
